enzyme_name: Succinate:quinone oxidoreductase (respiratory complex II / succinate dehydrogenase); catalytic flavoprotein subunit SdhA
organism_context: Bacteria (E. coli SdhABCD / FrdABCD) and mitochondria (SDHA-D); ubiquinone-8 is the bacterial/plant-type quinone
rationale: This is a heterooligomeric membrane complex (SdhA flavoprotein + SdhB Fe-S protein + SdhC/SdhD membrane anchors), not a fused multidomain chain, so the multi-subunit exclusion applies; the single catalytic succinate-oxidation site sits on the covalently FAD-bound SdhA subunit, and the quinone site in SdhC/D is part of the same electron-transfer reaction rather than a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: The entry is named 'fumarate reductase complex' but the equation uses ubiquinone-8 (Em' ~ +100 mV) against the fumarate/succinate couple (Em' = +30 mV), which favours the written succinate-oxidising (SQR) direction; the reverse flux is run by the distinct low-potential menaquinol-dependent FRD complex, so ModelSEED's '>' fits the ubiquinone form and the council's '<' appears to be anchored on the misleading FRD name.

enzyme_name: 7-dehydrocholesterol reductase (Delta7-sterol reductase, DHCR7)
organism_context: Vertebrates/plants/fungi (DHCR7 orthologues); the opposite-sense cholesterol 7-desaturase NVD/DAF-36 (EC 1.14.19.21) exists in insects and nematodes
rationale: KEGG R08131 is retired, but 'Provitamin D3' is C01164 = 7-dehydrocholesterol, so the cholesterol/7-DHC couple is the EC 1.3.1.21 reaction (KEGG R01456, cholesterol + NADP+ = cholesta-5,7-dien-3beta-ol + NADPH + H+), run by DHCR7 - a single-activity sterol Delta7-reductase (no literature search needed for this well-characterised monofunctional enzyme; identification made from the KEGG EC 1.3.1.21 record).
direction_note: DHCR7 physiologically runs the reduction 7-dehydrocholesterol + NADPH -> cholesterol as the terminal step of the Kandutsch-Russell cholesterol pathway, i.e. the reverse of the written direction; cholesterol -> 7-DHC only happens via the separate O2-dependent Rieske desaturase (NVD/DAF-36), and ModelSEED's equation has dropped NADP/NADPH entirely, so the forward call rests on an unbalanced half-reaction.

enzyme_name: Lycopene beta-cyclase (carotenoid beta-end group lyase, EC 5.5.1.19); fused phytoene synthase/lycopene cyclase CrtYB-AL-2-CarRA in fungi
organism_context: Bifunctional, genuinely fused single polypeptide in fungi (Xanthophyllomyces dendrorhous CrtYB, Neurospora crassa AL-2, Mucorales CarRA; KEGG ortholog K17841). Separate monofunctional enzymes in plants (LCYB), most bacteria (CrtY) and cyanobacteria/green sulfur bacteria (CruA/CruP); actinobacterial isorenieratene producers use a two-polypeptide CrtYc/CrtYd pair, which is a complex, not a fusion.
rationale: In fungi the enzyme that cyclises gamma-carotene to beta-carotene is a single chain carrying an N-terminal lycopene cyclase domain and a C-terminal phytoene synthase domain - two distinct catalytic activities (EC 5.5.1.19 + EC 2.5.1.32), confirmed by domain-resolved mutant analysis of Neurospora al-2. Per the protocol's lineage rule this counts as bifunctional even though plant and bacterial orthologues are monofunctional.
direction_note: Carotenoid beta-ring cyclisation is the committed, effectively irreversible step of beta-carotene biosynthesis and the fungal enzyme's partner phytoene-synthase domain pushes flux the same way; the 'decyclizing' EC systematic name is nomenclature convention, not evidence of physiological reverse flux, so the enzymology supports ModelSEED's forward call.

enzyme_name: Beta-lactamase (penicillinase, penicillin-G hydrolase, EC 3.5.2.6)
organism_context: Bacteria; serine (class A/C/D) and metallo (class B) beta-lactamases
rationale: KEGG R04318 names this 'penicillin-G hydrolase' under EC 3.5.2.6; beta-lactamases are single-activity hydrolases that open the beta-lactam ring (the regulatory sensor-transducer BlaR1 is a separate protein, not a fused second catalytic domain) - a confidently known monofunctional enzyme, no literature search required beyond the EC/KEGG assignment.
direction_note: Decisive for the conflict: KEGG writes this reaction as Penicillin G + H2O -> benzylpenicilloate, whereas ModelSEED's equation is the reverse (benzylpenicilloate -> H2O + Penicillin G). Beta-lactam ring hydrolysis is essentially irreversible, so the physiologically real direction is right-to-left as ModelSEED has written it - the council's '<' is correct and ModelSEED's '>' reflects a flipped equation, not reverse-running enzymology.

enzyme_name: unidentified - no enzyme is known to methylate S-adenosyl-homocysteine to S-adenosyl-L-methionine with 5-methyltetrahydropteroyltriglutamate
rationale: The written chemistry (SAH + 5-methyl-H4PteGlu3 -> SAM + H4PteGlu3) has no characterised catalyst: the real 5-methyltetrahydropteroyltriglutamate-dependent methyltransferase is cobalamin-independent methionine synthase MetE (EC 2.1.1.14), which methylates free homocysteine, and SAM is then made separately by methionine adenosyltransferase (MetK/MAT), so this record looks like a lumped or mis-substituted ModelSEED entry - reinforced by its synonym list, which mixes in wholly unrelated glucosyl-, fructosyl-, sulfo- and ribosyltransferases under the generic name 'Methyltransferase'.
direction_note: If the intent was the MetE step, that methyl transfer is physiologically irreversible in the methyl-donating direction (toward methionine/SAM), which would support '>'; but since the substrates as written are not MetE's, no enzymological direction call can be trusted for this record.

enzyme_name: none - model-specific NADH sink pseudo-reaction (the attached EC 1.8.1.4 points to dihydrolipoyl dehydrogenase, which does not catalyse this)
rationale: The entry's own synonyms declare it a 'Model-specific reaction, used to affect NADH levels'; NADH -> NAD+ with no electron acceptor is not a balanced chemical transformation and no protein catalyses it, so there is no enzyme to classify. The dangling EC 1.8.1.4 annotation refers to dihydrolipoyl dehydrogenase (lpdA/DLD), a monofunctional FAD flavoprotein that serves as the shared E3 subunit of the pyruvate, 2-oxoglutarate and branched-chain 2-oxoacid dehydrogenase complexes - a multi-subunit-complex component, not a bifunctional enzyme, and in any case not the catalyst here.
direction_note: Direction here is a modelling choice (a free NADH sink), not enzymology; neither '>' nor '<' has biochemical meaning, and because the reaction is redox-unbalanced the thermodynamic estimates that drive the ModelSEED call are meaningless for it.

enzyme_name: none - model-specific NADPH sink pseudo-reaction
rationale: As with rxn12950, the entry names itself 'Model-specific reaction, used to affect NADPH levels by converting NADP+ to NADPH' (BiGG FNADPH); NADPH -> NADP+ with no acceptor is not a real enzymatic transformation and carries no EC number, so there is no catalysing protein to classify.
direction_note: Direction is an arbitrary modelling convention for a redox sink rather than an enzymatic property; the 'gold' thermodynamic grade is spurious because the reaction is not redox-balanced.

enzyme_name: unidentified - KEGG itself flags R08847 as an 'unclear reaction'
rationale: The KEGG record for R08847 (3,4-dihydroxyphenylpropanoate <=> (R)-3-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl)lactate) carries the explicit comment 'unclear reaction', has no EC number, no KO/orthology assignment and no reference, and the two compounds differ by an oxygen atom, so this is not a single characterised enzymatic step.
direction_note: No enzyme and an unbalanced transformation, so there is no enzymology on which to base a direction; the mismatch here is between two ab-initio dG estimators, not between an enzyme and a predictor.

enzyme_name: Alcohol dehydrogenase (cytosolic NAD+-dependent class I ADH)
organism_context: Mammalian liver (trichloroethylene/chloral hydrate metabolism); KEGG assigns only the generic EC 1.1.-.- with the comment 'dehydrogenase'
rationale: KEGG R09149 gives only 'dehydrogenase'/EC 1.1.-.-, but the trichloroethanol/chloral couple is the well-documented ADH step of trichloroethylene metabolism, carried by class I alcohol dehydrogenase - a monofunctional zinc-dependent dehydrogenase; the enzyme identity is inferred from the chemistry plus the TCE toxicology literature rather than from a direct assay citation for this KEGG entry.
direction_note: In vivo the flux runs the opposite way to the written equation: chloral (as chloral hydrate) is rapidly reduced by ADH to trichloroethanol, which is the dominant urinary metabolite, so the oxidation direction ModelSEED calls forward is the minor one - the council's '<' matches the physiology even though the small negative dG'o favours '>'.

enzyme_name: unidentified - hypothetical glucosylation step of the (still unelucidated) salicortin pathway
organism_context: Populus / Salix (Salicaceae) salicinoid biosynthesis, MetaCyc PWY-6763
rationale: The complete salicinoid/salicortin pathway remains unresolved and MetaCyc's PWY-6763 steps carry no assigned protein; the nearest characterised catalysts are the Populus family-1 UDP-glucosyltransferases PtUGT71L1 and PtUGT78M1 (and SpUGT71L2), but these glucosylate salicyl benzoate rather than this HCC-ester intermediate, so no enzyme can be attached to this specific reaction.
direction_note: As written the reaction condenses free D-glucose with an aglycone and expels water, which no glycosyltransferase does (UGTs transfer from UDP-glucose), so both the dG estimate and the direction call are artefacts of placeholder stoichiometry rather than enzymology.

enzyme_name: unidentified - hypothetical dearomatisation step of the salicortin (HCC-moiety) pathway
organism_context: Populus / Salix salicinoid biosynthesis, MetaCyc PWY-6763
rationale: Conversion of the benzoyl group of benzyl benzoate into the 1-hydroxy-6-oxo-cyclohex-2-ene-1-carboxyl (HCC) moiety has no identified catalyst; D7-cinnamate labelling in Populus trichocarpa establishes only that the HCC moiety derives from cinnamate/benzenoid catabolism, and the characterised salicinoid enzymes to date are the BAHD acyltransferases PtBEBT/PtSABT and the UGT71L1 glucosyltransferase, none of which performs this step.
direction_note: The step as written dearomatises and oxygenates a benzene ring with no cosubstrate at all, so it is a lumped pathway placeholder rather than a one-enzyme reaction; the very large dG'o values (-71 to -97 kJ/mol) are for an unbalanced transformation and should not be read as a direction constraint.

enzyme_name: MaoC-like steroid side-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase ChsH1-ChsH2 (CasM-CasO in Rhodococcus)
organism_context: Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Rhodococcus jostii RHA1 cholesterol/steroid side-chain degradation (actinobacteria)
rationale: The C3-side-chain steroid hydratase of the last beta-oxidation cycle is a heteromeric MaoC-family enzyme built from two separate polypeptides, ChsH1 and ChsH2, forming a pseudo-heterodimeric alpha2beta2 complex with one active site - a multi-subunit complex, which the protocol excludes from 'bifunctional'; ChsH2 does carry a fused DUF35 domain, but it is non-catalytic and serves to recruit the Ltp2 aldolase for the next step.
direction_note: Decisive for the conflict: the enzyme is a hydratase and the catabolic flux is 3-oxo-23,24-bisnorchol-4,17(20)-dien-22-oyl-CoA + H2O -> the 17-ol (which MetaCyc's own reaction name reflects), so ModelSEED has the equation written as the reverse dehydration; the council's '<' matches the physiological beta-oxidation direction.

enzyme_name: unidentified - no enzyme has ever been isolated for the uracil -> 2-hydroxy-4-carboxypyrimidine step of lathyrine biosynthesis
organism_context: Lathyrus tingitanus (lathyrine biosynthesis, MetaCyc PWY-1)
rationale: The pathway rests entirely on 1970s radiotracer feeding work in Lathyrus tingitanus seedlings showing that [2-14C]uracil label ends up at C-2 of lathyrine via a preformed orotate-derived pyrimidine; no protein, gene or in vitro activity has been reported for any step, so the catalyst of this reaction is genuinely unknown.

enzyme_name: unidentified - the hypothesised benzoyl-CoA 2-hydroxylase of the PAL route to salicylate was never isolated, and the completed pathway bypasses it
organism_context: Plants (salicylate biosynthesis via the phenylalanine ammonia-lyase route)
rationale: No protein has ever been shown to hydroxylate benzoyl-CoA at C-2; the 2025 elucidation of the complete PAL pathway in rice and Populus shows that benzoyl-CoA is instead esterified to benzyl benzoate (peroxisomal benzoyltransferase OSD2) and the ring hydroxylation happens at the benzyl benzoate stage via the ER cytochrome P450 OSD3, with a carboxylesterase (OSD4) releasing salicylate - so this MetaCyc step is a superseded placeholder.
direction_note: As written the hydroxylation has neither O2 nor a reductant on the left-hand side, so the ~-35 to -39 kJ/mol estimates are for an unbalanced half-reaction; with no real catalyst and no cosubstrates, neither direction call is enzymologically supported.

enzyme_name: 12-oxophytodienoate reductase (OPR3; OPR1/OPR2 isoforms)
organism_context: Plants (Arabidopsis thaliana, Solanum lycopersicum) - jasmonate biosynthesis, peroxisomal
rationale: EC 1.3.1.42 is 12-oxophytodienoate reductase, a single-domain FMN flavoprotein of the Old Yellow Enzyme family with one (beta/alpha)8-barrel active site; its homodimerisation is a regulatory/self-inhibitory phenomenon (and recent work questions even that), not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Decisive for the conflict: OPR3 physiologically reduces 12-OPDA with NADPH to OPC-8:0 in jasmonate biosynthesis, i.e. right-to-left as ModelSEED has written it; the written equation additionally carries a spurious ADP product, which is what produces the absurd -334 to -452 kJ/mol dG estimates driving the '>' call.

enzyme_name: Delta14-sterol reductase (C-14 sterol reductase): TM7SF2 and lamin B receptor (LBR) in humans, Erg24p in yeast, FACKEL in Arabidopsis
organism_context: Vertebrates (two paralogues, TM7SF2 and LBR), fungi (ERG24), plants (FACKEL)
rationale: EC 1.3.1.70 enzymes carry a single NADPH-dependent sterol Delta14-reduction site; LBR's additional N-terminal nucleoplasmic Tudor domain binds lamin B and tethers heterochromatin, but that is a structural/scaffolding role, which the protocol's moonlighting exclusion keeps out of the bifunctional category - only the C-terminal sterol reductase domain is catalytic.
direction_note: The enzyme reduces the Delta14 bond (4,4-dimethyl-cholesta-8,14,24-trien-3beta-ol + NADPH -> 14-demethyllanosterol) in sterol biosynthesis, so the written oxidative direction is the reverse of the physiological one; as with the other sterol entries in this chunk the equation also carries a spurious ADP, inflating the dG estimate behind ModelSEED's '>'.

enzyme_name: Delta24-sterol reductase (24-dehydrocholesterol reductase, DHCR24 / seladin-1)
organism_context: Vertebrates (DHCR24, Bloch pathway); fungal/plant Erg4-DWF1 homologues of the same FAD-dependent sterol reductase family
rationale: EC 1.3.1.72 DHCR24 is a single-activity FAD-dependent sterol Delta24-reductase; its 'seladin-1' identity as a neuroprotective/anti-apoptotic and oxidative-stress-responsive protein is a cellular role attributable to its sterol product, not a second catalytic activity, so the moonlighting exclusion applies.
direction_note: DHCR24 physiologically reduces the side-chain Delta24 double bond with NADPH (5alpha-cholesta-7,24-dien-3beta-ol -> lathosterol), i.e. right-to-left as written; ModelSEED's forward direction is the reverse, and the equation's spurious ADP product is what drives the implausible -373 to -439 kJ/mol dG values behind the '>' call.

enzyme_name: unidentified - same hypothetical salicortin glucosylation step as rxn22709, with beta-D-glucose as the written donor
organism_context: Populus / Salix (Salicaceae) salicinoid biosynthesis, MetaCyc PWY-6763 (same MetaCyc RXN-12250 as rxn22709)
rationale: This is the beta-D-glucose variant of the same MetaCyc RXN-12250 placeholder; the salicortin pathway is still unelucidated and MetaCyc assigns no protein to this step, with the closest characterised candidates being the Populus UDP-glucosyltransferases PtUGT71L1/PtUGT78M1, which act on salicyl benzoate instead.
direction_note: Written as a dehydrative condensation of free beta-D-glucose with an aglycone - chemistry no glycosyltransferase performs - so the direction and the eQuilibrator dG that supports it describe the placeholder stoichiometry, not a real enzyme.

enzyme_name: Succinate:quinone oxidoreductase (respiratory complex II); catalytic flavoprotein subunit SdhA
organism_context: Bacteria and mitochondria; ubiquinone-9 is the common rodent/yeast-type quinone
rationale: Same enzyme as rxn09272 with ubiquinone-9 as the acceptor: a four-subunit membrane complex (SdhABCD), excluded from 'bifunctional' by the multi-subunit rule, with the single succinate-oxidation site on the covalently FAD-linked SdhA subunit.
direction_note: With a high-potential ubiquinone acceptor the succinate-oxidising direction is favoured, so ModelSEED's '>' is right for this quinone; fumarate reduction requires the low-potential menaquinol used by the separate FRD complex, which is what the entry's misleading 'fumarate reductase' name points the council toward.

enzyme_name: Succinate:quinone oxidoreductase (respiratory complex II); catalytic flavoprotein subunit SdhA
organism_context: Mammalian mitochondria (ubiquinone-10/ubidecarenone is the human quinone)
rationale: Same enzyme as rxn09272/rxn37562 with ubiquinone-10: the SDHA-SDHB-SDHC-SDHD complex is an association of four separate polypeptides, not a fused chain, so the multi-subunit exclusion applies and SDHA - which carries the covalent FAD and the succinate site - is monofunctional.
direction_note: In mitochondria complex II runs overwhelmingly in the written succinate-oxidising direction as a TCA-cycle and respiratory-chain enzyme; reverse (fumarate-reducing) operation needs a reduced quinone pool under hypoxia and is the exception, so ModelSEED's '>' is the better default here.

enzyme_name: Chloromuconate cycloisomerase (ClcB/TfdD/TcbD type, EC 5.5.1.7)
organism_context: Chlorocatechol-degrading proteobacteria (Cupriavidus/Alcaligenes eutrophus JMP134, Pseudomonas sp. P51) and Rhodococcus opacus 1CP (convergently evolved, non-dehalogenating)
rationale: Enzyme identity is inferred from the chemistry - the substrate/product pair is a chloromuconate/chloro-lactone cycloisomerisation of the modified ortho-cleavage chlorocatechol pathway that MetaCyc PWY-6093 belongs to - rather than confirmed from a record for RXN-9886; chloromuconate cycloisomerases are Mg2+-dependent enolase-superfamily octamers with a single active site (the chloride elimination some of them perform is part of the same cycloisomerisation, and the Rhodococcus 2-chloromuconate enzyme lacks it altogether).
direction_note: The catabolic flux is muconate -> lactone (cycloisomerisation), so the written ring-opening direction is the reverse of the pathway direction; the council's '<' therefore matches the physiology, while the near-zero group-contribution dG shows the step itself is close to equilibrium and carries little thermodynamic constraint.

enzyme_name: tRNA(Ile2)-agmatidine synthetase (TiaS)
organism_context: Archaea (characterised from Archaeoglobus fulgidus); the bacterial AUA-decoding counterpart is the unrelated lysidine synthetase TilS
rationale: TiaS installs 2-agmatinylcytidine at the wobble position of tRNA-Ile2 using agmatine and ATP, through a single novel Thr18-Cyt34 kinase domain (TCKD) that phosphorylates C2 of C34 before agmatine displaces the phosphate; the paper describes it as a 'dual protein and RNA kinase' because the same domain also autophosphorylates Thr18, but that is the same phosphoryl-transfer chemistry on a second substrate (and autophosphorylation), not a second distinct catalytic activity - hence monofunctional, with medium confidence because of that dual-kinase framing.
direction_note: The real reaction is ATP-dependent and driven irreversibly forward by ATP hydrolysis to AMP + pyrophosphate, and the physiological substrate is C34 within tRNA rather than free cytidine; ModelSEED's equation omits ATP entirely, so the wildly disagreeing dG estimates (+52 vs -80 vs -85 kJ/mol) are for a bare condensation and cannot adjudicate a direction that enzymology already fixes as forward.

enzyme_name: unidentified - organism-specific MetaCyc PGDB step (RXN1UA-51) in acyl-tetronate biosynthesis with no catalysing protein in the literature
rationale: The substrate and product are phosphorylated 4-acyl-tetronate (tetronic acid) intermediates bearing a 6-methyloctanoyl chain, but no PubMed or Europe PMC record names an enzyme for this desaturation, and the reaction comes from an organism-specific BioCyc PGDB rather than a curated MetaCyc core entry, so the catalyst cannot be identified.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous intramolecular condensation of the PaaZ ring-opening aldehyde
organism_context: Bacteria with the aerobic CoA-dependent phenylacetate (paa) catabolic pathway; the cyclic product is salvaged by TdaE in Phaeobacter/Burkholderia tropone and tropodithietic acid biosynthesis
rationale: This step is non-enzymatic: the oxepin-CoA ring-cleavage product is a highly reactive aldehyde that, if the aldehyde-dehydrogenase domain of PaaZ does not oxidise it immediately, condenses intramolecularly on its own to the stable cyclic 2-hydroxycyclohepta-1,4,6-triene-1-carboxyl-CoA, so there is no enzyme to classify (the relevant enzyme, PaaZ, is genuinely bifunctional - MaoC hydratase + NADP+ aldehyde dehydrogenase - but it catalyses the competing reactions, not this one).
direction_note: The cyclisation is spontaneous and effectively irreversible to a stable dead-end product - which is precisely why PaaZ's fused dehydrogenase domain must out-compete it in vivo - so ModelSEED's forward '>' is correct and the council's '<' is wrong here.

enzyme_name: unidentified - MetaCyc's 'daphnin transglucosylase' has no supporting record in PubMed or Europe PMC
organism_context: Daphne / Thymelaeaceae (MetaCyc PWY-7055, daphnetin modification)
rationale: Searches of PubMed and Europe PMC for 'daphnin transglucosylase' and for daphnetin glucosyltransferases in Daphne return nothing, so no protein, gene or assay can be attached; the MetaCyc name's parenthetical '(8-O-glucosyltransferase activity)' hints the curators split one putative protein's glucosidase and glucosyltransferase activities across entries - which, if real, would make it bifunctional - but there is no evidence either way, so 'unknown' is the honest call.
direction_note: The enzyme name implies a transglucosylation with daphnin (daphnetin 7-O-glucoside) as the glucosyl donor, whereas the ModelSEED equation substitutes free D-glucose and releases water; that condensation is not chemistry any glycosyltransferase performs, so the '>' call rests on placeholder stoichiometry rather than on the enzyme's real reaction.
